Summary: Scrum ceremonies — Sprint 1 — Repository, Tooling, and Architecture Foundation
Description:
Sprint Goal: Create the technical foundation for full-stack development and production deployment.

Production Gate: The repository must be clean, reproducible, and runnable by another developer from documented steps.

Sprint Review: Demonstrate frontend, backend, and database running locally.

Sprint Retrospective: Record setup problems, missing dependencies, and improvements for developer workflow.

Ceremonies: Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective.
Sprint: Sprint 1 — Repository, Tooling, and Architecture Foundation

Summary: Scrum ceremonies — Sprint 2 — Database Schema and Backend Foundation
Description:
Sprint Goal: Implement the core database schema and backend structure based on the KB data model.

Production Gate: Database must be version-controlled through migrations. Manual database changes are not allowed.

Sprint Review: Demonstrate database migration from empty database to working schema.

Sprint Retrospective: Record schema risks and any required corrections before adding business modules.

Ceremonies: Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective.
Sprint: Sprint 2 — Database Schema and Backend Foundation

Summary: Scrum ceremonies — Sprint 3 — Authentication, Users, Roles, and Access Control
Description:
Sprint Goal: Implement secure employee login and role-based access control.

Production Gate: No protected resource may be accessible without authentication and correct role authorization.

Sprint Review: Demonstrate login as Admin, Campaign Manager, BI Analyst, Product Manager, Compliance Officer, and Customer Service Agent.

Sprint Retrospective: Record authorization gaps and improve role-check consistency.

Ceremonies: Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective.
Sprint: Sprint 3 — Authentication, Users, Roles, and Access Control

Summary: Scrum ceremonies — Sprint 4 — Customer, Prospect, and Beneficiary Management
Description:
Sprint Goal: Build the CRM foundation for customers, prospects, and beneficiaries.

Production Gate: Customer data must use validation, pagination, soft delete, and role-based access.

Sprint Review: Demonstrate creating a policyholder customer and linking a grandchild/beneficiary.

Sprint Retrospective: Review whether customer fields are sufficient for segmentation and consent workflows.

Ceremonies: Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective.
Sprint: Sprint 4 — Customer, Prospect, and Beneficiary Management

Summary: Scrum ceremonies — Sprint 5 — Consent, Opt-Out, Do-Not-Contact, and Eligibility
Description:
Sprint Goal: Implement compliance-critical consent logic before campaign features.

Production Gate: Consent, opt-outs, do-not-contact, guardian consent, and eligibility must not be simulated.

Sprint Review: Demonstrate that a customer without valid consent is blocked from marketing eligibility.

Sprint Retrospective: Record whether the eligibility logic is centralized enough to avoid duplicated compliance logic.

Ceremonies: Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective.
Sprint: Sprint 5 — Consent, Opt-Out, Do-Not-Contact, and Eligibility

Summary: Scrum ceremonies — Sprint 6 — Product, Product Ownership, Product Change Requests, and Payments
Description:
Sprint Goal: Implement the product and policy-related data required for campaign targeting and reminders.

Production Gate: Product and ownership data must support product-expiration campaigns and segmentation.

Sprint Review: Demonstrate assigning a product to a customer and setting an expiration date.

Sprint Retrospective: Record whether payment and ownership records are enough for reminders and analytics.

Ceremonies: Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective.
Sprint: Sprint 6 — Product, Product Ownership, Product Change Requests, and Payments

Description:
Sprint Goal: Build the audience segmentation engine and preview logic.

Production Gate: Segmentation must never return a final campaign audience without eligibility checks.

Sprint Review: Demonstrate a segment for beneficiaries aged 18–35 without homeowner insurance and show eligible/excluded counts.

Sprint Retrospective: Record whether the criteria model is flexible enough for future campaign types.

Ceremonies: Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective.
Sprint: Sprint 7 — Segmentation Engine

Summary: Scrum ceremonies — Sprint 8 — Campaign Builder and Campaign Lifecycle
Description:
Sprint Goal: Implement the complete campaign draft, editing, submission, and review workflow.

Production Gate: Submitted campaigns cannot be launched before Compliance Officer approval.

Sprint Review: Demonstrate creating a campaign, submitting it, rejecting it, editing it, resubmitting it, and approving it.

Sprint Retrospective: Record whether campaign workflow is clear enough for non-technical business users.

Ceremonies: Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective.
Sprint: Sprint 8 — Campaign Builder and Campaign Lifecycle

Summary: Scrum ceremonies — Sprint 9 — Recipient Preview and Campaign Launch
Description:
Sprint Goal: Implement recipient generation, eligibility enforcement, and campaign launch.

Production Gate: A campaign launch must never bypass consent, opt-out, do-not-contact, duplicate, guardian consent, or approval rules.

Sprint Review: Demonstrate launching only an approved campaign and prove excluded contacts are not contacted.

Sprint Retrospective: Record any rule conflicts and simplify the eligibility logic if needed.

Ceremonies: Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective.
Sprint: Sprint 9 — Recipient Preview and Campaign Launch

Summary: Scrum ceremonies — Sprint 10 — Communication Tracking and Provider Adapters
Description:
Sprint Goal: Implement contact events and replaceable communication provider architecture.

Production Gate: Development may use mock email, but production must use a real configured provider or disable sending until configured.

Sprint Review: Demonstrate a launched campaign creating contact events and visible contact history.

Sprint Retrospective: Record what is still needed for real email/SMS provider integration.

Ceremonies: Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective.
Sprint: Sprint 10 — Communication Tracking and Provider Adapters

Summary: Scrum ceremonies — Sprint 11 — Follow-Up Tasks and Reminder Scheduling
Description:
Sprint Goal: Implement follow-up workflows, payment reminders, and product-expiration reminders.

Production Gate: Reminder logic must respect consent, payment status, expiration dates, and contact frequency limits.

Sprint Review: Demonstrate Green, Yellow, Red reminder lifecycle and product-expiration reminder generation.

Sprint Retrospective: Record whether reminder rules need configuration through system settings.

Ceremonies: Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective.
Sprint: Sprint 11 — Follow-Up Tasks and Reminder Scheduling

Summary: Scrum ceremonies — Sprint 12 — Analytics and Reports
Description:
Sprint Goal: Implement business dashboards, campaign metrics, and report exports.

Production Gate: Executive reports should use aggregated data where possible.

Sprint Review: Demonstrate a campaign analytics dashboard and export a campaign report.

Sprint Retrospective: Record whether metrics are accurate and whether any metric depends on external provider events.

Ceremonies: Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective.
Sprint: Sprint 12 — Analytics and Reports

Description:
Sprint Goal: Implement AI-assisted decision support without allowing AI to make final legal or marketing decisions.

Production Gate: AI must be decision support only. It must not override compliance approval, consent, opt-out, do-not-contact, or eligibility rules.

Sprint Review: Demonstrate AI recommending a product and explaining why, while requiring human approval before campaign use.

Sprint Retrospective: Record whether the AI feature is useful enough or should remain simple/rule-based.

Ceremonies: Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective.
Sprint: Sprint 13 — AI-Assisted Features

Summary: Scrum ceremonies — Sprint 14 — Audit Logging, Security Hardening, and System Settings
Description:
Sprint Goal: Harden the system for production readiness and accountability.

Production Gate: Sensitive actions must be auditable and production must not expose secrets or stack traces.

Sprint Review: Demonstrate audit log entries after role change, consent update, and campaign approval.

Sprint Retrospective: Record security gaps and prioritize them before release candidate.

Ceremonies: Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective.
Sprint: Sprint 14 — Audit Logging, Security Hardening, and System Settings

Summary: Scrum ceremonies — Sprint 15 — Frontend Professionalization and Accessibility
Description:
Sprint Goal: Make the application usable, professional, accessible, and role-aware.

Production Gate: A business user should be able to complete core workflows without developer help.

Sprint Review: Demonstrate login, customer creation, consent update, campaign creation, approval, launch, and analytics from the UI.

Sprint Retrospective: Record UI friction points and fix blocking usability issues.

Ceremonies: Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective.
Sprint: Sprint 15 — Frontend Professionalization and Accessibility

Summary: Scrum ceremonies — Sprint 16 — Full Test Suite and Quality Assurance
Description:
Sprint Goal: Verify the system against functional, non-functional, security, business-rule, and production-readiness requirements.

Production Gate: No production release if critical tests fail.

Sprint Review: Demonstrate the test suite and core workflow passing.

Sprint Retrospective: Record quality gaps and decide whether to release or add one hardening sprint.

Ceremonies: Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective.
Sprint: Sprint 16 — Full Test Suite and Quality Assurance

Summary: Scrum ceremonies — Sprint 17 — CI/CD and Deployment Automation
Description:
Sprint Goal: Automate build, test, packaging, and deployment preparation.

Production Gate: Main branch must not be releasable unless CI passes.

Sprint Review: Demonstrate a passing CI pipeline from a clean commit.

Sprint Retrospective: Record pipeline speed, reliability, and missing checks.

Ceremonies: Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective.
Sprint: Sprint 17 — CI/CD and Deployment Automation

Summary: Scrum ceremonies — Sprint 18 — Production Deployment and Operations
Description:
Sprint Goal: Deploy the system in a production-ready environment with operational safeguards.

Production Gate: Production release is allowed only after smoke tests, backups, security config, and critical workflows pass.

Sprint Review: Demonstrate deployed system, login, customer creation, consent update, campaign creation, approval, launch, and analytics.

Sprint Retrospective: Record deployment risks and post-release improvements.

Ceremonies: Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective.
Sprint: Sprint 18 — Production Deployment and Operations

Summary: Scrum ceremonies — Sprint 19 — Documentation, Demo, and University Report Evidence
Description:
Sprint Goal: Prepare the final project evidence, documentation, and university report material.

Production Gate: Documentation must allow another developer or evaluator to understand, run, test, and review the system.

Sprint Review: Demonstrate final report evidence and full demo flow.

Sprint Retrospective: Record lessons learned, Agile process evaluation, and future improvements.

Ceremonies: Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective.
Sprint: Sprint 19 — Documentation, Demo, and University Report Evidence
